sections.h2: Tax office, Supervisors and Chancery Clerk
sections.html:
Hancock County combines two jobs in one: the County Administrator also serves as Tax Assessor and Collector. The office is at 854 Highway 90 in Bay St. Louis, phone (228) 466-5791. The county's Tax Assessor page links to tax and fee information and a homestead exemption page.

  • Board of Supervisors: 854 Highway 90, Suite A, Bay St. Louis, phone (228) 467-0172.
  • Chancery Clerk and land records: 854 Highway 90, Suite B, phone (228) 467-5404.
  • Appeals of an assessment go to the Board of Supervisors, with the Chancery Clerk as the contact.

Call the office before you pay or mail a check, and confirm hours and payment methods.

All Mississippi counties use the same constitutional classes. The tax is true value times the assessment ratio times the millage rate. The county, each city and the school district set their own levies, which is why a house in Diamondhead and one in unincorporated Kiln can see different bills.

Mississippi property classes and ratios
ClassPropertyRatio
IOwner-occupied single-family home10%
IIOther real property15%
IIIPersonal property15%
IVPublic utilities30%
VMotor vehicles30%

The Department of Revenue posts combined county and city millage rates for 2012 through 2025 on its property tax data page, so look there for an official Hancock County number. Real property must be revalued at least every four years, and the assessor does not have to enter your home to do it.

The due date is February 1, and the tax falls on whoever owns the parcel on January 1. Bills go out in November and December. A February 1 that lands on a weekend or holiday rolls to the following Monday with no penalty or interest.

If tax stays unpaid, real property can be offered at the county tax sale. After a sale the owner has two years to redeem under Miss. Code Ann. 27-45-3. Property nobody buys goes to the State and is handled by the Secretary of State at 1-866-835-2637.

In practice, ask for a current payoff and any prior-year balance before you sign a contract. A title company will not close until delinquent taxes are cleared.

Ask the Board of Supervisors for a hearing, using the Chancery Clerk as your contact. An appeal normally must be filed by the first Monday in August before the taxes are due, so a homeowner who disagrees with a value cannot wait for the bill in December.

Bring evidence. Storm damage or a wrong square footage on the record are facts worth documenting. A refund for prior years can be possible when an appraisal had inaccurate information about home size, and the Chancery Clerk can explain how.

A buyer who plans to live in the home must apply in their own name. Applications go to the Tax Assessor between January 1 and April 1, and you do not reapply each year unless your status changes.

Owners 65 or older, and totally disabled owners who otherwise qualify, are exempt from taxes on the first $75,000 of true value. Eligibility is lost if the owner or spouse is out of compliance with state income tax laws or tags a vehicle in a different county from the home. A seller who has moved out should not keep claiming homestead on a house they no longer occupy.

Hurricane Katrina made its final landfall here on August 29, 2005, and local buyers still ask how a house fared. The storm destroyed nearly the entire first block off the beach, and homes as far as 10 miles inland flooded. Highway 603 south of Interstate 10 was submerged and the Highway 90 bridge at Bay St. Louis was wrecked. Bay St. Louis, Waveland, Pearlington, Diamondhead and Kiln all took heavy damage.

  • A buyer's insurer and lender will ask about flood zone and elevation, and a house with past water damage can be hard to finance.
  • Water covers 14% of the county's area, so many parcels sit near the shore. Check the county or FEMA flood maps to see where yours falls.
  • A cash buyer who purchases as-is can skip repair and insurance hurdles that sink conventional contracts, but should still be told about any known damage.

Sellers here may be dealing with a home that has storm or flood history, an inherited property or a house that has been vacant. Each situation has its own paperwork.

  1. Pull the deed and last tax statement and confirm the current owner on the roll.
  2. Ask the Tax Assessor and Collector for any prior-year balance.
  3. Confirm with the Chancery Clerk that no tax sale is recorded on the parcel.
  4. Gather repair and insurance records so a buyer can price the house honestly.

A cash sale lets the buyer take the house as it stands. You still need clear title and the current tax paid or settled on the closing statement. Confirm every figure with the county office before you rely on it.

Hancock County sits on the Gulf of Mexico at the Louisiana line, and its county seat is Bay St. Louis. It covers 553 square miles, and 79 of them (14%) are water, so much of the county is bayou, bay and marsh. The 2020 census counted 46,053 people.

The three cities are Bay St. Louis, Diamondhead and Waveland. Kiln and Pearlington are census-designated places, and smaller communities include Lakeshore, Clermont Harbor, Necaise and Napoleon. The John C. Stennis Space Center is in the county, which is part of the Gulfport-Biloxi metropolitan area. I-10, U.S. 90 and MS 43, 53, 603 and 607 are the major routes. School districts are Bay St. Louis, Hancock County and Picayune.

faqs.q: When are Hancock County property taxes due?
faqs.a: On or before February 1 under state law. If that date is a weekend or legal holiday, you can pay the following Monday without penalty or interest.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Hancock County?
faqs.a: The Tax Assessor and Collector, a combined office headed by the County Administrator, at 854 Highway 90, Bay St. Louis, phone (228) 466-5791. Call to confirm hours and payment methods.

faqs.q: How do I appeal a Hancock County assessment?
faqs.a: Ask the Board of Supervisors for a hearing, with the Chancery Clerk as the contact. An appeal normally must be filed by the first Monday in August before the tax is due.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Hancock County house damaged by a storm?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer can purchase a damaged house as-is. You still need clear title and any taxes paid or settled at closing, and you should disclose damage you know about.

faqs.q: How long can I redeem a Hancock County parcel after a tax sale?
faqs.a: Two years from the date of the tax sale under Miss. Code Ann. 27-45-3. The Chancery Clerk handles redemption notices and payments.
